findings.title: Acquired support within a failing portfolio

findings.mechanism: The focus verb carries taking for oneself. The neighboring wealth claim supplies an asset model; the covenant question tests durability; inheritance removes the claimant's possessions, and solitary arrival removes the support network. Together these context events turn the acquired gods into part of an imagined durable portfolio.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's religious objects also appear within the pericope's concrete picture of claimed supports being stripped away.
findings.containment: The focus still names gods taken for the hoped-for strength. The asset grouping is an attributed inference from 19:77-80, not a claim that the gods are literal property; the earlier wealth and child may concern only the singular claimant's possessions.

epistemic.reason: The Arabic surface, word indices, roots, and HFT roles match the lean pericope projection, but the HFT identity is legacy_unbound and its asset grouping is explicitly an inference.

findings.title: The intended support becomes an opposing party
findings.claim: The gods taken to serve as strength for their adopters become a counter-side that disavows the worship directed to them and stands against those adopters.

In 19:82, the same coming-into-state construction returns with the same plural participants while for them shifts to against them and strength shifts to opposition; the worship bond itself is also disavowed. The repeated form and changed direction make the support relation reverse.
findings.reader_payoff: The passage makes the collapse relational: the supposed support does not merely fail to help but becomes the other side of the relation.
findings.containment: The focus remains an account of what the adopters sought; 19:82 gives the reversal without erasing that aim. The counterparty facet does not imply equal power, and the attributed HFT reading may be a simple prediction rather than a deliberate mirror. The excluded enslavement branch is not claimed.

findings.title: A granted bond beside self-sought standing
findings.claim: The pericope places the focus's self-sought strength beside a later relation the Merciful makes for people of trust and sound action: affection is granted rather than assembled through adopted gods.
findings.mechanism: The focus purpose clause and indefinite abstract outcome are echoed by 19:96's beneficiary and abstract outcome. Agency changes: people take gods so that strength may be for them, while the Merciful makes affection for those who believe and act well.
findings.reader_payoff: The pericope makes two kinds of sought or granted benefit perceptible, with different agents and grounds.
findings.containment: The focus's stated aim remains intact; the later affection is a neighboring contrast, not a claim that it replaces or means the same as ʿizz. A live alternative is that wudd names divine love alone rather than public recognition.

epistemic.reason: The focus and 19:96 occurrences and structural echo are supplied; the status-economy interpretation is attributed and the source identity is legacy_unbound.

findings.title: The closing horizon removes every trace
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus's hoped-for standing can be heard as a bid for durable presence, while the closing horizon moves from destroyed generations to no sensed person and finally no faint sound.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries the ordinary strength-and-standing branch. The supplied final context orders destruction, failed sensory detection, hearing, and the faintest absent voice; this sequence contacts the possibility of durable standing with total loss of perceptible residue.
findings.reader_payoff: The macro horizon asks what any acquired strength can preserve when even the smallest trace of prior generations is absent.
findings.containment: The focus explicitly names strength and honor, not remembrance. The durable-presence link is an exploratory inference; the live alternative is that 19:81 concerns power during life only.

epistemic.reason: The HFT coordinates match the supplied focus and 19:98 roots, but the anti-erasure interpretation is expressly an inference and the reader identity is legacy_unbound.

findings.title: Judgment ownership sharpens the access boundary
findings.claim: The added Fātiḥa line names God as owner of the Day of Judgment; its ownership image gives the pericope's denial of owned intercession a specific judicial horizon around the focus's adopted supports.
findings.mechanism: The exact 19:87 trace names denied ownership over intercession; 1:4:1 names God as the owner, and 1:4:3 supplies the Day of Judgment. The shared ownership contact adds a concrete horizon to the access test without changing the focus's stated motive.
findings.reader_payoff: The limit on the hoped-for intermediaries is perceived beside an explicit assignment of judgment-day ownership.
findings.containment: This is an external overlay using 1:4 and the pericope's 19:87 trace. It does not claim that 1:4 discusses 19:81 directly or settles every question about intercession; the covenant clause and the focus's strength motive remain as stated.

epistemic.reason: The external and native root/word surfaces agree with the attributed HFT ownership contact, but the HFT reader identity is legacy_unbound and the external unit is a lean projection.

findings.title: Direct worship and help beside acquired strength
findings.claim: The added Fātiḥa address speaks to God alone in worship and in asking for help; beside the focus's adopted gods meant to be strength, it supplies a specific direct-reliance contrast.
findings.mechanism: The focus's plural deities carry the worship-object relation and ʿizz carries the hoped benefit. The external address independently pairs exclusive worship with asking aid from the same singular addressee, changing the focus arrangement into a contrast between acquired backing and direct reliance.
findings.reader_payoff: The support sought through adopted gods becomes legible beside a direct request for help addressed to God alone.
findings.containment: This is an explicitly added external overlay, not a lexical gloss or a claim that 1:5 refers to 19:81. It does not equate ʿizz with assistance or decide every theological implication of the Fātiḥa wording.

epistemic.reason: The focus morphology and exact external Arabic directly supply the worship, aid, and strength contact; the cross-ayah comparison is an interpretive overlay.
